description:
MEASURED s461aq while sizing #910.  `%p-flatten-list` returns
`(make-array 8 :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0)`, so every `(aref src-vec i)`
and `(length src-vec)` in p-list-='s expansion is a full call into SBCL's
hairy-data-vector path rather than an inline simple-vector reference.

HOW BIG: #910's first two attempts added ONE extra pass over that vector (1
length + k arefs + k eq tests per assignment) and it cost 0.11 s per 4e6
three-element list assignments â i.e. about as much as the TWO struct
allocations the whole task exists to avoid (base 1.811 s, keep-without-check
1.700 s, keep-with-a-separate-pass 1.810 s).  ~7 ns per generic aref.

WHAT TO TRY: have `%p-flatten-list` build into an adjustable buffer and hand
back a SIMPLE vector when it is worth it (`subseq` copies, so measure), or
declare the type at the p-list-= expansion sites so SBCL can pick the
specialised accessor.  Every list assignment in every program pays this, so
the win is broad if the copy is cheaper than the reads it saves.

The shipped #910 avoids the extra pass entirely (the commonality test rides
the flattener's own walk) â this task is the REMAINING cost, which is the
same for the stores.


SHIPPED s462as (round 19), commit 31920e0.  Runtime-only; no generation bump.

WHAT SHIPPED, in two halves that are both existing mechanisms (rule 11):

  * THE SIZED PATH.  When SRC is a plain element-storage vector (`%p-vec-data`,
    the s458ak helper) and every element passes the new `%p-flatten-sized-p`,
    the output length IS SRC's length, so the result is `(make-array n)` — no
    adjustable header, no fill pointer, no per-element capacity check, and no
    trim.  Everything else goes to `%p-flatten-list-general`, the old expanding
    walk, which now pushes with `%p-vpush` and returns a TRIMMED simple vector.
  * THE FTYPE PROCLAMATION.  `%p-flatten-list` always returns a SIMPLE-VECTOR
    and is declaimed to, which is what carries the fact into the GENERATED
    program's own compilation unit: the `aref`/`length` in p-list-='s expansion
    are inline now (verified: no HAIRY-DATA-VECTOR in the compiled call site).

THE CORRECTNESS POINT, and it is not obvious: THE CLASSIFICATION IS A SEPARATE
PRE-SCAN.  Deciding element by element and abandoning the half-filled result at
the first aggregate reads better and is WRONG, because `%p-assign-snapshot` is
not a pure read — a TIED element goes through FETCH and a MAGIC one through its
getter, so the elements already snapshotted run their user code again on the
re-walk.  Measured: with that form, `my $t; tie $t,'Cnt',7; my ($a,$b,$c) =
($t, @arr)` FETCHes TWICE where perl FETCHes once.  The second conjunct of
`%p-flatten-sized-p` (not a tie proxy, not a magic cell) is NOT what keeps
FETCH single — the pre-scan is; it is what makes the sized loop provably free
of Perl code, which is what licenses hoisting the data vector and the length.

MEASURED (A/B against 4c354bc's runtime, one machine, interleaved, min-of-K,
one transpile since emission is unchanged):
  oo (4e6 `my ($self,$x,$r) = @_` method entries)  1.7740 -> 1.5003   -15.4 %
  swap (4e6 `($a,$b) = ($b,$a)`)                   0.3609 -> 0.2527   -30.0 %
  arrhash -2.1 %, packunpk -1.6 %, hashkey -3.3 %
  gcdrec +0.1 %, arrfill -0.3 %, slices +0.7 %, sliceasgn -0.1 %,
  feread / ovlsub / listasgn5 flat within 0.7 %
The general path's trim shows up NOWHERE: the +2.6 % / +5.2 % a first run read
on gcdrec and sliceasgn was the small-N noise floor and is gone at 5x N.

WHAT NOT TO RETRY: returning a trimmed simple vector from the ADJUSTABLE build
in every case (the task's own first suggestion).  Measured in isolation, k=3,
4e6 cycles: build-adjustable + generic reads 0.1770 s, build-adjustable + trim
+ inline reads 0.1790 s — the trim costs slightly more than the reads it saves,
because a three-element source is read three times and copied once.  The win
comes from not building the adjustable vector at all (0.035 s).

GUARD: Pl/t/aassign-01.t 42 -> 44, INVERSE-GUARDED (with the rejected
element-by-element form the FETCH row reads 2; with the sized predicate
answering T for everything the aggregate row stops flattening).
subject: p-list-='s source vector is ADJUSTABLE, so every element read pays a generic AREF
